hero.description:
Kampong Ayer, or the Water Village (Malay: Kampong Ayer) is an area of Brunei's capital city Bandar Seri Begawan that is situated over Brunei Bay. 39,000 people live in the Water Village. This represents roughly ten percent of the nation's total population. All of the Water Village buildings are constructed on stilts above the Brunei River.
Built entirely of stilt houses and wooden walkways, this cluster of 42 villages housing more than 30,000 inhabitants is the world's largest water village. Antonio Pigafetta refer to it as the 'Venice of the East'.
The Water Village is really made up of small villages linked together by more than 29,140 meters of foot-bridges, consisting of over 4200 structures including homes, mosques, restaurants, shops, schools, and a hospital. 36 kilometers of boardwalks connect the buildings. Private water taxis provide rapid transit. Most of these taxis resemble long wooden speed boats. From a distance the water village looks like a slum. It actually enjoys modern amenities including air conditioning, satellite television, Internet access, plumbing, and electricity. Some of the residents keep potted plants and chickens. The district has a unique architectural heritage of wooden homes with ornate interiors. 
Development

As par of His Majesty's plans to improve the standard of living for the population in Kampong Ayer, King Hassanal Bolkiah decreed to build modern, two story stilt house made of concrete in the center of the Kampong Ayer around the years of 2013-2014 and the project continue on. These houses would be given to the people in need of new house, and not wishing to live on land [Wikipedia.org]

gallery.filename: Royal Customs Wharf in Brunei Town 1961 01.jpg
gallery.title: File:Royal Customs Wharf in Brunei Town 1961 01.jpg
gallery.source: Royal Customs Wharf in Brunei Town 1961 01
gallery.description:
Approximately 5,000 people gathered at the Royal Customs Wharf in Brunei Town on the morning of 11th December 1961 to bid farewell with the message "Selamat Berkhidmat kepada Tanah Air" ("Serve the Homeland Well") to 195 future soldiers of the Brunei Malay Regiment.
Before the recruits departed from Brunei, they had the opportunity to shake hands with the Honourable Dato Setia Marsal bin Ma’un, the Chief Minister of Brunei. The Chief Minister delivered a speech offering valuable advice to the recruits at the gathering.
Following this, Begawan Mudim Haji Adnan, the Kadhi of Brunei, recited a prayer for their safety, accompanied by the call to prayer (azan) by Mudim Haji Wasli.

These photographs were taken at the Royal Customs Wharf in Bandar Brunei before the future Brunei Malay Regiment recruits departed for Labuan. Another scene captured in Labuan on the evening of 11th December 1961 shows the recruits boarding the vessel Keningau to sail to Singapore.

gallery.filename: "Perlis" carrying Bruneian pilgrims to Singapore in 1959.jpg
gallery.title: File:"Perlis" carrying Bruneian pilgrims to Singapore in 1959.jpg
gallery.source: "Perlis" carrying Bruneian pilgrims to Singapore in 1959
gallery.description: The docks in Brunei Town were crowded with family members and relatives of the pilgrims departing Brunei on 21 April 1959. Before the ship set sail, farewell speeches and prayers for safety were recited by religious officials. Pictured above is the ship Perlis, carrying the pilgrims to Singapore, as it raised anchor and departed from the dock.

gallery.filename: "SEA EXPRESS" arrived in Brunei waters on Saturday, 9th April 1966.jpg
gallery.title: File:"SEA EXPRESS" arrived in Brunei waters on Saturday, 9th April 1966.jpg
gallery.description: "SEA EXPRESS" is the name of this ship that arrived in Brunei waters on Saturday, 9th April 1966, docking at the Royal Customs Wharf in Bandar Brunei at midday. This marks the second time the ship has arrived in Brunei Town. The ship, a cargo vessel, measures 258 feet in length and weighs 1,600 tons. Compared to the weights of other large ships that have arrived at the Bandar Brunei port and docked at the Royal Customs Wharf, this ship is significantly heavier, as most of those ships weigh approximately 1,000 tons each.
